title: Safety Signs: Shapes & Colours
whatItIs: Safety signs use shape and colour to tell you what's banned, what's dangerous, what you must do, and where exits, first aid and fire equipment are.
keyFacts: Red circle with a diagonal bar = prohibition: you must not do it. Black pictogram on white.
Yellow triangle with black edging = warning: be careful, there's a hazard.
Blue circle with a white pictogram = mandatory: you must do it, eg wear PPE.
Green rectangle or square = escape routes, exits and first aid. Red rectangle = fire-fighting equipment.

keyFacts.text: Employers MUST provide and maintain safety signs where a risk can't be avoided or reduced in other ways.

visual.caption: The five kinds of safety signboard

items.title: Prohibition: red circle and bar
items.text: Black pictogram on white. Don't do it, eg No smoking.

items.title: Warning: yellow triangle
items.text: Black pictogram and black edge. Be careful, eg Danger: electricity.

items.title: Mandatory: blue circle
items.text: White pictogram on blue. You must, eg Safety helmet must be worn.

items.title: Escape or first aid: green rectangle
items.text: White pictogram on green. Exits, escape routes, first aid.

items.title: Fire-fighting: red rectangle
items.text: White pictogram on red. Extinguishers, hoses, fire alarms.

items.title: Words on signs
items.text: Text can be added, but a fire exit sign with words only isn't acceptable.

a.label: Prohibition (red circle)
points: Red edge and diagonal bar on white
Tells you what you must NOT do

b.label: Mandatory (blue circle)
points: Tells you what you MUST do

onTheTest.question: What does a round blue sign with a white picture of a safety helmet mean?
onTheTest.why: Mandatory signs are round, with a white pictogram on blue. They prescribe specific behaviour, such as wearing PPE.

onTheTest.question: Which sign shows the way to an emergency exit?
options: White pictogram on a green rectangle
Black pictogram on a yellow triangle
White pictogram on a blue circle
White pictogram on a red square
onTheTest.why: Emergency escape and first-aid signs are rectangular or square, with a white pictogram on green.

traps: Red appears twice: a circle with a bar means don't; a red rectangle marks fire-fighting equipment.
Yellow warns of a hazard: it means be careful, rather than giving an order.
Signs don't replace other controls: they're used where risks can't be avoided or reduced otherwise.
